candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p. 26 / PDF p. 30: apply infection-prevention principles and facilitate appropriate and safe use of equipment/PPE
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — respiratory PPE / N95 extended use
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish extended use of an N95 respirator from limited reuse and unsafe sharing or continued use of a contaminated respirator.

options.A: The same N95 is worn for repeated close-contact encounters with several patients without removing it between encounters
options.B: The same N95 is removed after each encounter, stored, and later donned again by the same worker
options.C: An N95 is shared between multiple health care workers during the same shift
options.D: A disposable N95 is worn indefinitely even after it becomes soiled or contaminated

candidate.rationale: Current NIOSH/CDC guidance defines extended use as wearing the same N95 respirator for repeated close-contact encounters with several different patients without removing the respirator between encounters. B describes limited reuse, which involves doffing and later redonning the respirator. Respirators should not be shared, and contaminated or otherwise unsuitable respirators should be discarded.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Extended use means wearing the same N95 for repeated patient encounters without removal between encounters; this differs from limited reuse, in which the respirator is doffed and redonned.
candidate.source_document_title: Strategies for Conserving the Supply of N95 Filtering Facepiece Respirators
candidate.source_locator: Extended use of N95 respirators as respiratory protection: definition; Limited re-use of N95 and other disposable respirators: reuse requires removal/donning between encounters; discard criteria
candidate.source_organization: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), CDC
candidate.stem: When a health care facility implements extended use of N95 respirators as a supply-conservation strategy, what does 'extended use' mean?
